Theme

Latin word

aliquandō

adverb

ever (asking about a time not fixed); at some time; sometimes, now and then (as against never)

In this lexicon

  • ever

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.8.1: vīdistīne aliquandō Clitumnum fontem?; Sen. Ep. 72.8: vīdistī aliquandō canem …?

  • sometimes

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 83.6: aliquandō dormīsse mē sciō, aliquandō suspicor; Plin. Ep. 9.36.6: vēnor aliquandō

Notes

  1. 1aliquandō: long final o (Lewis & Short aliquandŏ). A compound of quandō, which de Vaan gives with a long final vowel (p. 507, s.v. quī); Festus records an older form quandōd (Lewis & Short s.v. quando). The Latinitas loci write aliquandō throughout, and the libellī quandō.
  2. 2aliquandō: long final o (Lewis & Short aliquandŏ). A compound of quandō, which de Vaan gives with a long final vowel (p. 507, s.v. quī); Festus records an older form quandōd (Lewis & Short s.v. quando). The Latinitas loci write aliquandō throughout, and the libellī quandō.

Examples

  • vīdistīne aliquandō Clitumnum fontem?

    have you ever seen the spring of Clitumnus?Plin. Ep. 8.8.1

    In the entry for ever

  • aliquandō dormīsse mē sciō, aliquandō suspicor

    sometimes I know I’ve slept, sometimes I only suspect itSen. Ep. 83.6

    In the entry for sometimes
